whatWasUnexplained: 860714a measured the transvection diameter as 2n in six of seven cases and 2n+1 at Sp(4,2), offering the self-duality of W(3,2) as company but no mechanism
lengthVersusResidue: a transvection has residue 1, so length >= residue always; computing both on matrices, length = residue almost everywhere with an anomaly set at residue + 1

theMechanism.qOdd: a small anomaly set whose extreme point is central, removed by projectivisation, leaving diameter 2n
theMechanism.qTwo: -I = I so there is no centre, PSp(4,2) = Sp(4,2), and a 178x denser anomaly set survives, leaving diameter 2n + 1
theMechanism.sp43Extreme: exactly one element at length 5 and it is -I = diag(2,2,2,2), residue 4
theMechanism.reading: the doily is not accidentally worse; every other case is rescued by its centre and the doily has none

correctionToMyFraming: 860714a reported the sweep on the projective action without saying so, leaving 'the latency law is 2n' ambiguous between the matrix and projective groups; on matrices Sp(4,3) is also 5. The law is about PSp, which is the architecturally right group since machine states are projective points, but the qualifier belongs in the statement
boundary: exact and exhaustive over every element of both groups, residue by rank(g - I) and length by full BFS; the identification of the single Sp(4,3) extreme element as -I is by direct comparison. The claim that odd q always rescues itself this way is NOT established -- verified at q = 3 and consistent with the earlier sweep. tau_2 is untouched
